newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Wednesday were inactive, with packers still bidding $66.00 per cwt with the bids passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.
"I guess its going to be a waiting game," one Kansas feedlot manager said.

Several feedlot managers said packers had enough cattle left from last week's active sales to wait another day before booking cattle for next week. Packers reportedly were waiting as long as possible to see what happens with CME live cattle futures.
If cattle futures turn sharply lower, it could scare a few owners into selling fed cattle at $67.00, which would be below their expectations, one feedlot manager said.
Cattle owners had been expecting fed cattle to trade at $68.00 Wednesday or Thursday, which would be steady with last week's top but up $1.00 from the bulk of last week's sales.
Outlooks for firm fed cattle prices also could be dampened by continued mixed beef prices this week, particularly if demand remains soft, some sources noted.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $0.11 per cwt to up $0.25 on 249 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
